messages:
alex: Quick sync 1: post-launch backlog trim for Search v2. We shipped last week; telemetry shows two classes of issues: (A) regressions causing incorrect top results (P1s from support), (B) polish/enhancement asks from power users. Need rubric: what gets a hotfix vs goes into next minor release?

maria: Noted. UX feedback mostly asks for snippet highlights and a clearer fallback. Those are enhancements imo.

kevin: From infra/eng: regressions are often model/feature toggles. If it's a correctness regression affecting >1% of queries for an enterprise tenant, hotfix runway = 24h. Otherwise, batched into the 2-week sprint.

alex: Proposal: criteria = impact (customer count + %queries), severity (P1/P2), and revert complexity. If impact >= 1% AND P1 customer -> hotfix. Otherwise next cycle. Thoughts?

dana: Support agrees on 1% threshold. Also want an SLA-driven opt-in for customers that want immediate rollbacks.

leo: Adding telemetry note: we can compute tenant-level mismatch delta vs baseline. I'll add a metric: `search.top1_mismatch_delta` and alert when >1% over 30m.

kevin: Good. Also add automated canary checks pre-swap: sample 500 golden queries per tenant group. Fail -> block rollout. We didn't have that for v2.

alex: OK. Operational items: 1) define alert + playbook, 2) rollback runbook, 3) triage path (support->oncall->eng lead->pm). Who owns each?

maria: I can draft the playbook copy for customers and internal comms.

kevin: I'll own rollback runbook and add the canary gate to the deploy pipeline. ETA 3 working days.

leo: I'll wire the metric and alert this afternoon, then create a dashboard.

release-bot: New checklist created: deploy-gates/search-v2-canary. Status: pending.

alex: Great. Now about backlog prioritization: we have 18 items labeled `search-v2:postlaunch` (mix of bugs+enhancements). My suggestion: split into Hotfix candidates (meets hotfix criteria), Sprint scope (next 2 weeks, high ROI), and Long tail. I'll assign owners after we label.

maria: Can we get customer signal attached to each ticket? e.g., who requested, # tenants impacted, and contact person. That'll help prioritize.

kevin: Agreed. Also include estimated engineering hours (T-shirt sizing).

alex: I'll run a quick triage session at 14:00. Agenda: review top 10 tickets by impact, decide hotfix vs backlog, assign owners. Please bring rough estimates.

dana: Support will bring the P1 cases and sample golden queries for each.

leo: I'll provide the mismatch deltas and a recommended rollback candidate list.

maria: One more scope negotiation note: product would prefer the snippet highlight enhancement in the next minor release because it materially improves conversion. If engineers push back on capacity, we can prototype a client-side fallback first.

kevin: If it's client-side, dev effort drops to ~1.5d. If server-side, ~5d. Call it out during triage.

alex: Perfect. Post-triage outcomes: We'll publish a public changelog + customer comms for any hotfixes. For all deferred enhancement asks, we'll create a timeline in the roadmap and notify requesters.

release-bot: Triage meeting created: #calendar 14:00 today. Invitees: alex, kevin, maria, dana, leo.

alex: Thanks team. If anyone spots a P1 while I'm in the triage please ping me directly. Closing thread for now; notes and actions to be added to the triage doc: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/SEARCH-TRIAGE-1791 :white_check_mark:
